title: When the order of bird calls matters
review_depth: Primary-paper methods, results and figure captions reviewed via author-uploaded text; interpretive commentary also consulted. No replication.
finding: Japanese tit playback experiments link call combinations and order to distinct receiver responses.
limitations: This supports a bounded interpretation in this species. Commentary distinguishes compositionality from stronger human-like systematicity; general language ability is not established.
lesson: Test a proposed meaning against receiver behavior and carefully matched controls.
next_review: Ask a qualified researcher which inference and controls could transfer to the chosen pilot.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.
study_snapshot: 21 birds in the first playback experiment; 34 in the ordering experiment.
First experiment: within-bird call components, combined calls and background control, with randomized treatment order.
17 birds per condition: natural versus reversed sequences, with other acoustic features matched.
Scanning and speaker approach, rather than an AI-generated verbal interpretation.
review_locator: Suzuki et al.: Methods, Experiments 1–2; Figures 3–4. Phillips & Wilson: opening argument on systematicity.

title: Patterns inside sperm whale codas
review_depth: Primary study summary in founding audit; full-text methods review pending.
finding: Analysis of sperm whale codas describes contextual and combinatorial acoustic structure.
limitations: Conversational context and structural variation are not an English vocabulary or evidence of unrestricted translation.
lesson: Model temporal structure while keeping claims about meaning separate from claims about acoustic patterns.
next_review: Review the segmentation, individual identities and contextual definitions before reproducing a result.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: A birth, a group, and changing vocal styles
review_depth: Primary study summary in founding audit; full-text methods review pending.
finding: A reported sperm whale birth connects changing vocal styles with an observed social event.
limitations: A single event offers a valuable observation, but cannot establish a general call dictionary or causal interpretation.
lesson: Attach synchronized behavioral context to sound, and retain the event as the unit of analysis.
next_review: Identify which interpretations could be tested in independent events.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: NatureLM-audio: a useful starting point
review_depth: Official model card and project documentation; Hugging Face revision 77855d9b0acd039f90798dcf0861f626bfefbd6f recorded. No inference run.
finding: NatureLM-audio provides a foundation-model approach to describing and classifying biological sounds.
limitations: Descriptions are predictions, not verified animal intentions. The reviewed model lists CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; parent-model terms also matter. A paid deployment has not been cleared.
lesson: Inspect a frozen release, its training data and license before using it in an evaluation or paid product.
next_review: Compare a permitted model against a simple baseline on independently labeled recordings.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: BirdNET: identification before interpretation
review_depth: Official repository and license/review documentation reviewed for the audit.
finding: BirdNET supplies bird-sound identification tools and a human review workflow for detections.
limitations: Identification does not establish meaning. Main package code is MIT and listed models are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; separate STM32 artifacts use Apache-2.0. Check the exact release.
lesson: Reuse existing identification and review capabilities where they fit instead of assuming a new platform is necessary.
next_review: Choose an exact artifact, inspect its terms, and measure errors on the intended recordings.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Perch: reusable representations of animal sound
review_depth: Official model card, repository migration notice, Hoplite README and frozen model configuration reviewed; no inference run.
finding: Perch supplies acoustic embeddings for downstream classifiers. The current practical tooling route is Perch-Hoplite.
limitations: Listed model terms are Apache-2.0, but task performance, training-data overlap and the exact downloaded bundle remain unverified. CPU and GPU variants differ.
lesson: Consider a frozen embedding baseline once the species, labels and data rights are established.
next_review: Verify the CPU artifact, preprocessing and runtime on permitted recordings before selecting it for an experiment.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: DolphinGemma and shared signals
review_depth: Official announcement reviewed; not an independent replication.
finding: DolphinGemma models patterns in dolphin sounds. The related CHAT work uses learned shared signals in human-dolphin interactions.
limitations: Learning a shared interface and translating spontaneous natural communication are distinct scientific tasks.
lesson: Choose which question a pilot is trying to answer before selecting the interface or model.
next_review: Keep natural-call interpretation and taught-symbol experiments in separate protocols.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: What bark classification can tell us
review_depth: Primary abstract and PDF Experimental Setup paragraphs reviewed; no reproduction or full data audit.
finding: Human-speech-pretrained Wav2Vec2 improved performance on selected dog-vocalization classification tasks.
limitations: Grounding uses four selected, stranger-related categories mixing vocal form and context. These results do not establish broad emotional or language translation.
lesson: The paper groups dogs across folds for context, breed and sex tasks; individual-dog recognition uses a different split. Match each evaluation to its intended claim.
next_review: Inspect household/session dependence and context labeling before treating this as a passive phone benchmark.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.
study_snapshot: 74 dogs; 16,789 segments across 14 labels, including non-dog sounds.
Ten-fold dog-grouped evaluation for context, breed and sex; identity recognition uses a different split.
62.18% accuracy versus 56.37% majority baseline: +5.81 percentage points.
Paper offers dataset and baselines by request; redistribution permission is not established.
review_locator: Published pages 16481–16484: Dataset, Experimental Setup, Grounding, Table 4 and Limitations.

title: Giving parrots a choice to connect
review_depth: Published PDF pages 4–10 and limitations reviewed; Table 2–4 layout checked. No independent reanalysis.
finding: Nine parrots used a caregiver-assisted video-call interface; the study reports greater engagement during the live phase.
limitations: Live always preceded playback. Reciprocity, caregiver cues and variable devices also complicate interpretation. Engagement is not a direct welfare or language measure.
lesson: Preserve the animal’s ability to stop, separate caregiver impressions from behavior, and account for condition order.
next_review: Review design and table-level inconsistencies with a specialist before adopting quantitative claims.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.
study_snapshot: Nine home-kept parrots over six months.
Six live sessions followed by six playback sessions; conditions were not counterbalanced.
Call initiation, engagement duration and caregiver interviews/questionnaires.
Behavior-specialist training, ongoing review and stopping provisions formed part of the study.
review_locator: CHI 2024 published version: sections 3–7, pages 4–11; Tables 2–4 on page 9.

title: Learned buttons and receiver responses
review_depth: University study report and vendor description reviewed; primary paper review pending.
finding: Research-team reporting describes appropriate responses by trained dogs to selected soundboard words.
limitations: This is evidence about responses to learned cues, not unrestricted conversation or a natural canine-language translation.
lesson: A learned shared interface needs different evaluation from an acoustic classifier.
next_review: Review cue controls and distinguish comprehension evidence from spontaneous production claims.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Plants emit signals we can measure
review_depth: Indexed primary-paper abstract reviewed; full-text methods review pending.
finding: The reported experiments describe airborne sounds from plants under stress and informative differences in recordings.
limitations: Informative emissions do not, by themselves, establish intentional communication or human-like language.
lesson: Measure a biological signal without converting a model-generated narrative into a scientific claim.
next_review: Review instrumentation and environmental controls before treating a sound as plant-derived.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: When another organism responds
review_depth: Primary PDF indexed abstract and publication-history excerpt reviewed; publisher direct access challenged. Full methods and supplements remain pending.
finding: Reported moth egg-laying preferences change with plant-sound playback and whether a real plant is present.
limitations: The reported hearing-control result supports a bounded interaction. Context changes the observed preference; this is not general plant conversation.
lesson: Receiver behavior is a stronger test of biological relevance than signal classification alone.
next_review: Read the complete protocol, replication structure and hearing controls with a specialist before proposing any intervention.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Fungal electricity needs careful controls
review_depth: Methods discussion and critique reviewed for the audit; no independent replication performed.
finding: Measurement work and critiques highlight difficulties in separating fungal electrical activity from environmental artifacts.
limitations: A detected pattern or analogy to words is not evidence of a semantic language.
lesson: Instrumentation and controls must come before language claims or a translation interface.
next_review: Keep fungi in the reading program until a qualified collaborator defines a feasible measurement question.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Start with tools researchers already use
review_depth: Official tool documentation reviewed for the audit.
finding: Arbimon, BORIS and BirdNET review tools already cover parts of acoustic analysis, behavioral annotation and detection review.
limitations: Feature availability does not prove an unmet product need or interchangeability between annotation formats.
lesson: Interview researchers using real workflows. An upstream contribution may be more useful than another platform.
next_review: Attempt one end-to-end annotation/export task and document a concrete gap before building an integration.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: A benchmark is only as useful as its labels
review_depth: BEANS task configuration and BEANS-Next card, displayed metadata and license description reviewed. No full data audit or experiment.
finding: Public benchmarks cover different tasks: the BEANS dog labels identify individuals, while BEANS-Next includes acoustic-description tasks.
limitations: These labels do not automatically provide observed behavior or intended meaning. BEANS-Next lists noncommercial terms and source-specific licenses. Training overlap is unresolved.
lesson: Select the scientific question first, then verify that the dataset measures it and supports an independent evaluation.
next_review: Inspect a relevant component, original annotations, group structure and rights after choosing the pilot question.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: A usable parrot dataset starts with its labels
review_depth: Primary abstract/introduction and official repository documentation reviewed; selected scripts and the 2020 annotation CSV inspected. Full statistical methods, supplemental methods and audio not reviewed.
finding: The study reports vocal individuality in monk parakeets. Its public repository provides code, bird identifiers and behavioral notes. Our metadata sample has 808 annotation rows; 752 contain behavior text.
limitations: Rows are not necessarily individual calls. The 176 distinct nonempty behavior strings mix visible actions, vocal events and interpretations. Missing identities, uncertainty and audio/session linkage require review. Caller identity is not translation.
lesson: Keep source recordings, independent behavior labels and subject/session groups linked. Audit labels before selecting a model.
next_review: Inspect selection-table joins, normalize only observable behaviors, assess annotation reliability and evaluate whether enough independent groups remain.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: AVES and AVEX: reuse an encoder before training one
review_depth: AVES abstract and official AVES/AVEX READMEs, including embedding examples and the AVEX license declaration. No model execution or checkpoint audit.
finding: Self-supervised audio encoders learn from unlabeled recordings. AVEX provides a common interface for extracting features and fitting small supervised classifiers.
limitations: Useful features or benchmark scores do not establish call meaning. Pretraining overlap, sample-rate choices and checkpoint rights need checking for the exact experiment.
lesson: Compare a frozen encoder plus a simple classifier with acoustic and context-only baselines before considering expensive end-to-end training.
next_review: Pin an AVEX revision and one checkpoint; inspect its model card, terms, pretraining overlap and frequency coverage before a bounded evaluation.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

reuse.asset: AVEX feature-extraction API; AVES/BirdAVES model family
reuse.rights: AVEX declares MIT for code. Checkpoint and training-data terms are separate and remain unapproved.
reuse.experiment: On an approved dataset, compare a frozen representation plus linear classifier against simple acoustic features with the same held-out sessions.

title: BIRB: test on the sounds your app will actually hear
review_depth: Primary paper v2 introduction, benchmark overview and Table 1; repository BIRB entry. Detailed metrics and full experiments still need review.
finding: BIRB tests retrieval from passive soundscapes using examples from focal bird recordings, including rare and held-out species.
limitations: These are retrieval and species tasks. They do not validate behavior labels, conversation or performance on a phone beside a pet.
lesson: Treat a clean recording and a noisy stationary phone as different evaluation conditions. Keep the search examples and test audio independent.
next_review: Review the task construction and metrics sections, then check each candidate dataset’s license and overlap with model pretraining.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.
study_snapshot: Rank soundscape recordings using a few labeled examples.
Focal recordings for training versus passive soundscapes for evaluation.
Table 1 separates validation, artificially rare and held-out species sets.

reuse.asset: BIRB task design and Perch benchmark code
reuse.rights: Repository declares Apache-2.0 for code; each underlying dataset requires its own terms check.
reuse.experiment: Report separate results by recording setting and independent session, plus precision among the clips a human is asked to review.

title: DAS: build on an existing annotation workflow
review_depth: Official introduction, repository README and bird tutorial through proofreading. The primary performance paper and current package were not evaluated.
finding: Deep Audio Segmenter connects manual labels, model training, automatic proposals and human correction in an existing audio workflow.
limitations: Suggested labels still need checking. A quick-start training split is not a validation protocol for our intended species or new recording conditions.
lesson: Keep model suggestions separate from accepted observations. Test file interoperability and reviewer effort before building another full annotation editor.
next_review: Inspect the exact DAS import/export schema and run a synthetic round trip before proposing an adapter.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

reuse.asset: DAS graphical annotation and proposal-review workflow
reuse.rights: Repository declares Apache-2.0 for code. Example audio, trained models and dependencies need separate checks.
reuse.experiment: Exchange a synthetic WAV and interval labels, then compare whether event boundaries and labels survive the round trip.

title: Bat calls: context comes from observation
review_depth: Primary Materials and Methods sections on housing, monitoring and classification tasks via PMC. Full statistics, supplementary analyses and raw data not reviewed.
finding: This study paired bat social calls with synchronized video to label caller, recipient, circumstances and subsequent behavior.
limitations: The main analysis used 14,863 calls from seven adult females. Many recordings were excluded when identification was uncertain. Captive social calls and specialized ultrasonic recording do not establish phone or wild-population performance.
lesson: Collect context independently of sound interpretation; document uncertain identities and exclusions instead of filling them with confident guesses.
next_review: Inspect cross-validation and identity/context controls before treating these data as a template for a held-out-animal experiment.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.
study_snapshot: Trained observers used video; uncertain caller assignments were excluded.
250 kHz audio sampling with specialized ultrasound microphones.
review_locator: Prat et al. (2016), Materials and Methods: Bat housing and monitoring; Classification tasks.

reuse.asset: Synchronized context annotation and explicit exclusion rules
reuse.rights: Paper access does not grant rights to an entire recording archive. No recordings acquired.
reuse.experiment: Before modeling, have two reviewers independently label a permitted sample and report agreement and unknown identities.

title: animal2vec: learn from rare calls and quiet intervals
review_depth: Primary abstract and official README, including recording setup and dataset link. Edmond files, statistical methods and model checkpoints not inspected.
finding: animal2vec targets sparse, unevenly distributed animal sounds. Its companion MeerKAT resource includes precisely timed meerkat vocalization annotations.
limitations: The documented recordings largely come from animal-worn devices; others used nearby directional microphones. They are not an unattended-phone benchmark. No transfer result has been measured by Talk2Nature.
lesson: Keep background intervals in an approved evaluation set. Testing only retained loud clips cannot measure what the detector missed.
next_review: Review event metrics and individual/day split construction; resolve dataset access and exact audio/annotation licenses.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

reuse.asset: animal2vec training code; linked MeerKAT dataset
reuse.rights: Repository declares MIT for code. Dataset and checkpoint terms are not verified here; acquisition remains pending.
reuse.experiment: Use independently annotated continuous audio to measure missed events and false alarms per hour, including quieter calls.

title: Elephant calls: pair promising findings with their critiques
review_depth: Selected discussion and playback methods in the author-organization PDF; Dryad landing page. The 2026 reanalysis was located through a publisher excerpt and related-work listing, not read in full.
finding: The 2024 study combines acoustic classification with receiver-response experiments to investigate individually directed calls.
limitations: Name-like is a bounded interpretation, not a recovered vocabulary. A 2026 reanalysis questions statistical evidence from the classification analyses; that dispute is not resolved by this note.
lesson: Maintain competing explanations and later critiques beside the original claim. Behavioral evidence and classifier results require separate assessment.
next_review: Read the full reanalysis, compare the exact null models and seek any author response before adopting the naming claim.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.
study_snapshot: 17 subjects; most received calls from the same caller directed to themselves versus someone else.
Trial scoring was blind to condition.
The later statistical critique needs a full methods comparison.
review_locator: Author-organization PDF pp. 4 and 10 (discussion and playback methods); publisher reanalysis excerpt.

reuse.asset: Matched receiver-response comparison; linked analysis/data deposit
reuse.rights: No audio, figures or code republished. Deposit contents and separate reuse terms remain to be inspected.
reuse.experiment: Write down alternative explanations and an appropriate null model before making any claim about a signal’s meaning. No playback is proposed for the public app.

title: Put the sound back into its scene
review_depth: SuperAnimal abstract, introduction and dataset sections reviewed; SLEAP publisher summary and SimBA paper index and official project description reviewed. No code or model execution.
finding: Pose tracking and supervised behavior tools offer building blocks for connecting a call to visible movement.
limitations: Keypoints are estimates. Occlusion, identity swaps, unfamiliar species and camera angles require evaluation. Quadruped or mouse checkpoints cannot be assumed to work on parrots.
lesson: Compare audio-only, video-only and combined models against independently made behavior labels.
next_review: Review exact checkpoint licenses, target-species coverage and synchronization error before testing. Hold out entire animals and sessions.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Plants have channels beyond sound
review_depth: Primary abstract, introduction and selected results/methods passages reviewed; supplementary data not reanalysed.
finding: Laboratory Arabidopsis imaging connects particular airborne leaf volatiles with calcium responses and defense-related gene expression.
limitations: The measurements use specialized reporters and imaging. Ordinary phone video cannot reveal these intracellular signals or decode a plant’s intention.
lesson: Select the sensor for the channel being studied: chemistry, physiology and sound need different instruments.
next_review: Have a plant physiologist review a passive monitoring question and its environmental controls.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: A slow signal needs a different clock
review_depth: Primary PDF abstract and Methods, pages 1–3, reviewed, alongside existing cataloged measurement caveats; independent replication and full statistical review pending.
finding: A 2026 study reports time-ordered electrical spikes across eight channels in one oyster-fungus specimen recorded for about fifteen days.
limitations: Channels from one specimen are not independent biological replicates. Timing structure does not decode meanings; shuffled-data comparisons do not replace substrate and instrument controls.
lesson: Fungal work needs electrodes, environmental logging and long recordings, not a phone microphone alone.
next_review: A qualified mycologist and electrophysiologist should design replication and artifact controls before any collection.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: When “words” are an analogy
review_depth: Author preprint abstract and existing cataloged critique reviewed; full methods and data reanalysis pending.
finding: An electrical-spike study applies word-like grouping and language statistics to fungal recordings.
limitations: Statistical resemblance does not establish a vocabulary, a receiver, a referent or a conversation.
lesson: Treat a proposed communication code as a hypothesis that needs functional tests.
next_review: Ask whether a pattern predicts an independently measured outcome beyond environmental and measurement confounds.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Beautiful patterns need independent tests
review_depth: 2006 primary abstract, 2008 replication abstract and 2009 journal letter on p. 83 reviewed. Raw images, full protocols and later literature not systematically assessed.
finding: Emoto and collaborators reported differences in aesthetic ratings of ice-crystal photographs after distant-intention treatments.
limitations: A published critique identifies bottle-level non-independence. The follow-up shares investigators. These reports do not establish that water understands words or that thoughts reliably change crystal structure.
lesson: Curiosity is welcome; a striking image is not a validated communication mechanism.
next_review: If revisited, preregister independent bottle-level replication, blinding, all-image inclusion and objective outcomes. This is not the basis of Talk2Nature’s biology program.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Parrot owners can contribute; species still matter
review_depth: Abstract, selected results and data-collection methods; no supplement or raw-table analysis.
finding: An owner survey covered 877 parrots from 73 species and found variation in reported mimicry.
limitations: Owner reports and recruitment bias limit inference. Learned human sounds are not a decoded natural vocabulary.
lesson: Our proposal: retain species and individual identity; distinguish observed behavior from owner interpretation.
next_review: Review the questionnaire and deposited table, then test a small species-specific observation codebook.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Budgerigars: a candidate, not a shortcut
review_depth: Primary abstract/highlights, versioned deposit/license and file inventory; one checksum-pinned MAT container inspected. Full methods and statistical audit pending.
finding: The study examines individual vocal signatures. Our local inspection of one 1.49 MB deposit file found 15 call structures with raw, filtered and normalized arrays: 82,315 raw samples in total. The stored sample-rate value is 44,101 and has not been corrected or independently verified.
limitations: One smallest-file convenience sample is not a representative corpus. The inspected structure has no explicit independent visible-behavior annotation field. Caller, acquisition units and intervention status remain unverified; laboratory results do not validate passive phone recordings or call meaning.
lesson: Our provisional choice is a single-species budgerigar feasibility pilot, conditional on access and expert review.
next_review: Resolve the unusual stored sample-rate value, recording conditions, caller/session linkage and untreated subsets against full methods before proposing acoustic reuse.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Cats: useful labels, limited reuse
review_depth: Version 1.0.2 record, API rights and naming conventions; paper abstract only.
finding: CatMeows documents 440 sounds from 21 cats with context, cat, owner and session identifiers.
limitations: CC BY-NC 4.0 is not general commercial permission. Elicited contexts should not become app instructions; files were not acquired.
lesson: Our proposed evaluations should hold out households and animals, not just random clips.
next_review: Review recording dependence and split design; resolve project-specific reuse rights before a benchmark.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Pig calls: inspect what the labels actually mean
review_depth: Primary indexed abstract/results excerpts and repository description/API; full methods not reviewed.
finding: The paper analyzes calls across production contexts. The open Soundwel subset contains 6,888 calls in 17 categories.
limitations: The deposit excludes restricted slaughterhouse recordings. Context-associated valence is not a translated sentence or validated household emotion detector.
lesson: Our proposed use is a separate farm-research comparison, with its own setting and evaluation.
next_review: Audit pig/farm/session identifiers and labeling assumptions before designing any reuse experiment.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Frog choruses: several callers, one recording
review_depth: Data records, selected validation sections, repository description and code README; no replication.
finding: AnuraSet provides multilabel frog-call data and a reproducible baseline for species identification.
limitations: Identification is distinct from communication meaning. The paper says CC0 while the versioned record API says cc-by; acquisition is deferred.
lesson: Our app retains mixed scenes and uncertainty. Future evaluations should test rare classes and new recording settings.
next_review: Resolve dataset rights, inspect site/time dependence and pin the code before downloading a benchmark.
